title: Freddie Keppard with his handkerchief, Jimmy Noone and King Oliver's soft playing
summary: Keppard covered his horn with a handkerchief and was powerful; Lil thought him better than Oliver; Hunter knew him little.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Now, tell me if I'm jumping too far, but I was going to ask you about the Sunset.
Sunset? You're jumping way too far.
I am.
Uh-huh. Yeah. Now, I'm at the De Luxe now.
Uh-huh.
And that's where Freddie Keppard was. You remember, Freddie Keppard was very famous.
Yeah.
He was a marvelous -- but he never got the break that he deserved.
Now, was Louis Keppard his brother?
I don't know. That I can't say.
Uh-huh.
I don't know. The only one I knew, Freddie Keppard.
Uh-huh.
And he had some -- and Jimmy Noone.
Yes.
Jimmy Noone.
Now, they always say about Freddie Keppard that he was afraid others would steal his style.
So he wouldn't play.
So that he played with a handkerchief --

Always. Always. That's right. That's right. He covered his horn with a handkerchief all the time. He sure did. And he -- well, I won't say that because I want to tell about Joe Oliver, how soft he would play. But Freddie Keppard, oh, he was a marvelous trumpet player. You called them trumpets then, didn't you? You didn't call them cornet players. Trumpet players you called them.
Well, Lil told me that she thought Freddie was actually better than --
Joe.
Joe.
Oh. I put Joe's picture in here for you.
Oh.
Uh-huh. Yes. Yes. I thought so, too. Because as I say, he --
Powerful, right?
He was powerful. He could play and you couldn't hear him -- like I'm talking to you?
Uh-huh.
You couldn't hear him if he didn't want you to. But if he wanted you to, you could hear him to 135th Street.
Uh-huh.
He was powerful. And he had some
marvelous musicians with him. Now, there's Jimmy Noone, and who else was with him? Wasn't Tommy Ladner with him?
I don't recall Tommy Ladner being with him. It's possible.
Who --
But what was he like?
Freddie Keppard?
Yes.

I never had much dealings with him, but he always seemed to be a very nice fellow, but he seemed to stay to himself more or less. I don't remember having very much to do with him, because as I say, he -- I used to say, 'Hello, Freddy,' and keep going. One of those things. I never had much to say to him.
